edition.name: Dharmabindu, a work on Jaina philosophy, by Haribhadra, with the commentary of Municandra
edition.publisher: Royal Asiatic Society of Bengal, Calcutta (printed at the Baptist Mission Press)
edition.editor: Luigi Suali; partly revised and seen through the press by Chintaharan Chakravarti
edition.digitized_by: Structured for the portal by Vyom A. Shah

blurb: Haribhadra's compact manual of the Jaina way of life, in eight adhyāyas of terse sūtras. It moves from the general duties of a householder to the special vows, the fitness for and discipline of ascetic life, and the fruits of dharma up to liberation. It is read here with the full vṛtti of Municandrasūri.
about: Haribhadra opens with a verse promising a bindu, a drop drawn from the ocean of scripture, and defines dharma as conduct that follows the uncontradicted word of the Jina and is joined with maitrī and the other three attitudes. He then divides it into the dharma of the householder and that of the ascetic. Adhyāyas 1–3 treat householder dharma in its general and special forms, including the aṇuvratas, guṇavratas and śikṣāpadas with their transgressions. Adhyāyas 4–6 treat renunciation and the life of the ascetic, and adhyāyas 7–8 the fruit of dharma.

Municandrasūri's vṛtti opens each sūtra with a short lead-in, which the reader shows above the sūtra's commentary. It then glosses the sūtra word by word and supports it with verses cited from Jaina and Brahmanical sources.

Suali's Bibliotheca Indica edition was begun in 1908, stalled after 1921, and completed by Chintaharan Chakravarti in 1940. It counts the opening and closing verses of each adhyāya as sūtras and prints the closing iti apart from the sūtra, unlike the 1924 Ahmedabad edition. Where the printed sūtra number in this text is a slip, the reader numbers the sūtras in sequence and notes the printed number.
